title: Man dies after fight with police: A suspect in a home invasion died two days after a struggle with a police officer near the crime scene in east Vancouver.
article: An autopsy was performed Wednesday on a man who died two days after a fight with a police officer behind a home where there had been a home invasion.
Police said Jeffrey Michael Berg, 37, of Vancouver collapsed and stopped breathing during the fight with an officer Sunday night in the 4800-block of Slocan Street near Kingsway.
He was resuscitated by paramedics but did not regain consciousness before he died on Tuesday. Results of the autopsy are expected later this week.

Vancouver police Constable Anne Drennan said police received a 911 call about 9:30 p.m. Sunday that two men wearing stocking masks and scarves over their faces had beaten down the front door of a house with a dumb-bell.
She said a marijuana-growing operation was found in the same house in June.

When the masked men broke in, a man and two children escaped out the back door. Three women and a child were left inside, where they were herded into a room while the invaders searched the rest of the house.
The man who had escaped from the house ran to another house and called 911.

A veteran dogmaster officer and his canine partner, who were responding to a false alarm home invasion on nearby McHardy street, took the call and spotted the masked suspects and two other men in car in the lane behind the home that had been broken into.

"The suspects' vehicle took off in the lane and our vehicle followed it immediately and rammed it," Drennan said. "The vehicle spun when it was rammed and ended up being pinned up against a garage wall on the side of the lane."
Drennan said Berg got out of the broken passenger window of the suspects' car, climbed over the hood and started fighting with the police officer, who had drawn his gun.
Drennan was not able to give any other details of the fight, except that it was "not long at all" and no weapons were used.
"There's a struggle, there's a fight, and suddenly the suspect collapses and stops breathing."
She could not say where the police dog was during the fight, but said the only visible signs of injury on Berg were a small cut above his eyebrow and an abrasion on one side of his face.
The three other suspects were taken into custody. One was released without charge, and the two others have been charged. Drennan said nothing was taken from the house.
Edward Borden, 38, of Vancouver was charged with break and enter, unlawful confinement and wearing a mask in the commission of an offence.
David Morrison, 27, faces the same charges, as well as dangerous driving and violating parole.
"What happens now is that our major crime section conducts an investigation into the death and a separate investigation into the home invasion," Drennan said.

"When there's a death involved, the major crime or serious crime section has to deal with a police-involved death -- they have to conduct a thorough investigation as there would be into any other death \[involving police\] that could be related possibly to a fight or an accident."
